_readme: Color schemes of the UI. This file is the source -- the UI
reads it at startup and sets the values as CSS custom properties on
:root. A new scheme therefore needs NO code change: add an
entry here, reload the page, done.
'forge' is the baseline and is complete. Every other scheme lists only
its DEVIATIONS; those are layered over the baseline. Anyone creating their
own scheme therefore only writes what should be different.
The role colors (r-*) are checked against the dataviz methodology with
scripts/validate_palette.js, not chosen by eye -- the
measured values are listed per scheme under 'geprueft'. Anyone changing
colors should remeasure: node validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode dark

forge.label: forge_app (default)
forge.note: The tuned working look: muted, for long screen sessions.

verified.colour_vision: weakest pair E-Trace/funnel dE 0,5 (protanopia) -- colour is deliberately only a hint here; identity is carried by the block label and the legend
verified.screenshot_note: For a screenshot in PPT/HTML use the 'contrast' theme: there the colour carries on its own.

contrast.label: High contrast (for screenshots)
contrast.note: For an image embedded in PPT or HTML and projected: brighter role colours, stronger fill, thicker frames and wires. Also holds up when the projector eats the midtones.

verified.colour_vision: weakest pair dE 8,6 (deuteranopia) -- above the target of 8; normal vision weakest pair dE 16,2
verified.abweichung: Lightness band of the methodology deliberately exceeded upwards -- the higher brightness IS the purpose of this theme.

print.label: Light / print
print.note: Light background for paper, handouts or a bright slide. Dark, strong role colours -- on white, darkness carries the contrast, not brightness.

verified.colour_vision: weakest pair dE 8,5 (deuteranopia); normal vision dE 17,8

mono.label: Greyscale (B/W print)
mono.note: No colour. For black-and-white printing and as a probe whether the drawing stays readable without colour -- if something drowns here, it relies on colour alone in the colour schemes, and that is a defect.

verified.method: deliberately NO colour coding -- the roles differ only in brightness; identity is carried by the label
verified.screenshot_note: Only the side path is below 3:1 -- intended, it should recede. The remaining six roles sit between 4,08:1 and 18,37:1, adjacent steps are separated by a factor of 1,23 to 1,47.
